rationale: Preprint of rank 2 same four-person Parkinson subthalamic sleep neural-recording study; electrical stimulation pulses are not dietary legumes and no pinto-insomnia comparison.
Four Parkinson patients with externalized deep-brain electrodes had stimulation pulses and sleep-stage electrophysiology measured; pulses are not bean intake. Same family as rank 1.
Electrical stimulation and impedance during sleep in healthy adults; cardiac pulses are physiological, Parkinson disease is mechanistic background and no pinto exposure.
Parkinson case with insomnia receives transcranial and vagus magnetic stimulation pulses; abstract describes mood, constipation and cognitive follow-up, no legume intervention.
Arabica coffee beans decaffeination and neuraminidase assay; caffeine-related insomnia is background and coffee beans are not pinto.
Healthy-human limb immobilization and brain imaging signal pulses; Parkinson and sleep are mechanistic comparisons, no food or pinto study.
Narrative preprint on caffeine in tea and coffee; coffee beans are not pinto and no measured pinto-insomnia comparison.
Eighteen Parkinson patients randomized real versus sham magnetic stimulation pulses; sleep-scale changes occurred equally in both arms, no pinto or dietary intervention.
Evidence review of gastric electrical stimulation for gastroparesis and obesity, including Parkinson as a possible cause and general dietary advice; no pinto-insomnia comparison in abstract.

Oral isolated eugenol (50/100 mg/kg/day) in acrylamide-toxic rats; gait score, foot splay and rotarod reportedly improved. Locomotor/motor endpoint is adjacent, but toxin-induced neuropathy rather than PD, and no ground allspice exposure.
Tick-control essential-oil study; eugenol is among chemical constituents and locomotor appendage damage is an arthropod toxicity outcome, not mammalian/PD walking.

Oral isolated eugenol pharmacokinetic/permeation work in rats and dopamine release in PC12 cells; no gait or motor-behavior test, PD population/model, or allspice fruit. Mechanistic route context only.

Original J-STAGE PDF body/methods/results inspected in full. Oral isolated eugenol 25/50/100 mg/kg/day in MPTP mice (n=6/group), pre/co-treatment or post-treatment; timed narrow-beam walking, locomotor counts, catalepsy, rearing and rotarod. Beam crossing improved with all pretreatment doses and worsened with all post-treatment doses. Strongly relevant to constituent/model/timing only; not culinary ground Pimenta or human gait. See original pages 155–159 and saved PDF Vora-2022-01026.pdf.

Review of eugenol for brain disorders including Parkinson disease; secondary source and isolated compound, with no allspice food exposure or new direct human walking comparison. Can guide citations, not primary outcome evidence.
Eugenol component of holy basil/clove tested against SARS-CoV-2 spike/ACE2; no Parkinson or gait/motor endpoint.
Oral isolated eugenol in rat spinal-cord injury reported functional/motor recovery; injury model, not PD, ground allspice or a clinical Parkinson walking endpoint.
Gavage eugenol in rat osteoarthritis model measures nociception/pain, not PD gait or walking slowness.
Locomotor assay in triatomine insect vectors after monoterpene exposure; no PD, mammalian motor function or allspice dietary intervention.

Primary abstract for isolated oral eugenol plus zingerone/levodopa in 6-OHDA mice: no improvement in levodopa-related abnormal behavior and increased striatal DA depletion after post-lesion treatment. Timing cautions against transferring a single eugenol direction; abstract lacks detailed gait estimates and does not test ground allspice.

Dietary eugenol/isoeugenol enrichment ameliorated acrylamide-related locomotor deficits in Drosophila; non-mammalian toxicant model and isolated spice actives, not ground allspice or Parkinson walking.
Rat odor-span/working-memory experiment; Parkinson appears as disease context in abstract, but no allspice/eugenol exposure or walking endpoint.
Narrative review on spice-derived nutraceuticals and neuroprotection includes Parkinson disease and clove/eugenol context; no ground Pimenta-specific human walking result, and not primary evidence.
Cumulative index chapter lists Parkinson among many topics but gives no allspice exposure, study or measured motor outcome; lexical collision.

Saudi 2024 foodborne botulism cases had dysarthria but original Methods and Discussion identify contaminated mayonnaise from a burger chain, not sardines; pre-existing neurological disorders were excluded.

Original preprint Tables 5 and Methods report examiner-detected dysarthria 24.9% in 197 residents exposed to methylmercury through unspecified contaminated seafood vs 1.6% in 130 controls; no species, grilled preparation, Parkinson cohort or formal intelligibility score. Subsequent peer-reviewed report PMID38133424 is same analysis.
Parkinson speech-diagnosis algorithm uses virtual sardines as the prey in sailfish optimization; sardine is not food administered or consumed.
Gut-brain-axis review mentions sardines as a dietary omega-3 source; communication is biological signaling, with no measured sardine exposure and Parkinson speech-intelligibility outcome.
